Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-27
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Mark Davis (CTO - Silverline), Elena Ruiz (Head of Platform), Samir Patel (Security), Rosa Kim (Product)

Summary (auto):
Discovery for Dedicated capacity. Customer currently using hosted APIs but evaluating reserved GPUs for latency/cost/isolation. Key topics: throughput (sustained qps), burst strategy, VPC/private deployment, SOC2 & KMS, autoscaling and observability. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark plan, 2-week trial.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh we'll do a quick intro from our side then jump into your current stack and what you're trying to accomplish with dedicated capacity. i'm jordan, account exec for redwood.
[00:18] Mark: hey jordan, thanks. i'm mark, cto at silverline. quick heads-up - we're on a tight timeline, Q4 budget, want to decide by mid-october.
[00:28] Jordan: got it, mid-oct. priya will be on for technical stuff. priya, intro?
[00:32] Priya: hi all, priya raman, solutions eng. i focus on perf/infra and helping teams size dedicated clusters and run benchmarks.
[00:39] Elena: i'm elena, platform lead - we run k8s on eks and have 3 availability zones in us-east. we currently use openai for chat + embeddings, but costs are getting out of hand and we need stronger isolation for PII.
[00:55] Samir: samir - security. main reqs: SOC2, audit logs, sso/saml, customer-managed keys and network isolation. also data residency for EU customers.
[01:08] Jordan: perfect - sounds like dedicated capacity is in scope. can you give a rough sense of traffic shape? sustained qps, burst, token counts, typical sequences?
[01:20] Elena: our baseline right now is about 100 qps for chat generation across our platform, with p95 latency target of ~250ms for short replies. we get spikes during batch reconciliation jobs and marketing campaigns up to 600 qps for ~30-90 minutes. embeddings workload is smaller qps but heavy in token count - sometimes 3k tokens per request.
[01:45] Priya: ok that's helpful. when you say 250ms p95, is that end-to-end or just token latency?
[01:51] Mark: that's end-to-end, from our API gateway to response.
[01:54] Priya: good. for dedicated, we usually size for sustained qps and then offer burst capacity via queued workers or burst nodes; we can also do autoscaling with buffer capacity to maintain the latency SLO.
[02:06] Jordan: do you have any hard isolation needs? multi-tenant separation or compliance reasons?
[02:12] Samir: yes we need logical separation from other tenants and control over keys - customer managed KMS is necessary. we also need the ability to run in our VPC, or at least a dedicated VPC peering model, not public endpoints.
[02:25] Priya: Redwood Private supports VPC-deployed control plane and private deployments. For Dedicated (hosted dedicated) we offer VPC peering and private endpoints. small typo in our docs sometimes says 'Redwood Dedcated' so ignore that.
[02:37] Rosa: quick Q - what about model variants? we sometimes want to route to a smaller model for low-cost fallback.
[02:45] Priya: yes we support smart routing - policy-based. you can route by latency, cost or region; if primary model isn't available we can fallback to a compatible variant.
[02:53] Mark: pricing is critical. we looked at a couple of numbers from other vendors - give us an idea of the commitment levels for reserved GPUs and burst pricing.
[03:03] Jordan: sure. high-level: reserved capacity is monthly commit - e.g., 4 x A100-equivalent nodes for dedicated pool with options for burst nodes billed at a higher per-hour rate. i'll send a formal quote, but ballpark for fully managed reserved nodes starts at... (mumbles) i'll follow up in email.
[03:20] Mark: ok we need a cost model so we can compare to hosted api per token costs.
[03:25] Priya: operationally, our runtime supports automatic batching, prefix/KV cache, and quantization-friendly execution paths which reduce per-token cost. we'll include expected token/sec and cost-per-1k calc in the follow-up.
[03:38] Samir: about encryption - do you support HSM or customer-managed keys with rotation?
[03:43] Priya: we integrate with customer KMS providers for envelope encryption; HSM integrations are available for Private deployments. for hosted dedicated we support customer-managed keys and key rotation per policy.
[03:54] Elena: network - we prefer VPC peering with private endpoints and strict IP allowlist. can you do that?
[03:59] Priya: yes, VPC peering or privatelink-style endpoints. we'll propose network architecture doc.
[04:06] Jordan: any constraints on model sizes? we saw some customers run both generation and embeddings on the same pool - is that recommended?
[04:14] Priya: depends. embeddings with long sequences can hog memory; recommend separate pools for heavy-embedding jobs or using burst nodes dedicated to embeddings. we can also use quantized variants to fit larger models.
[04:25] Mark: how quick is autoscaling? we can't have cold-starts that blow latency.
[04:30] Priya: autoscaling is policy driven; for Dedicated we do warm standby nodes and fast spin-up of extra workers. typical warm-up is minutes not tens of minutes; for instant spikes we recommend reserved burst nodes or keeping a small buffer of idle capacity.
[04:43] Mark: what telemetry do we get? token-level latency, tracing, per-route cost?
[04:48] Jordan: Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks and error analysis. you can export logs to your SIEM, and we provide trace ids to correlate.
[05:00] Rosa: our product team wants canary rollouts and A/B serving for model updates. supported?
[05:06] Priya: yes - rollouts, canaries, A/B tests and automatic fallback policies are supported. you can pin model versions and do gradual traffic shifts.
[05:14] Samir: security question: audit logs retention, and who can access logs? we need role-based access controls and SIEM forwarding.
[05:21] Priya: RBAC is supported; audit logs can be forwarded to your logging infra and retention is configurable as an add-on. we'll include SOC2 and compliance docs.
[05:30] Mark: curious about performance baseline - can you give a rough tokens/sec number for an A100-equivalent node for typical chat model?
[05:39] Priya: rough ballpark: for a 4k context chat model on A100-equivalent, you might see ~150-250 tokens/s per node for generation workloads depending on beam/temperature etc. with batching and KV cache that improves for repeated prefixes. for embeddings throughput we often see higher tokens/sec but memory pressure increases.
[06:02] Mark: so to hit our 100 qps with 250ms p95, any thumbs up on number of nodes?
[06:10] Priya: if your median token per request is ~60 tokens, and assuming 200 tokens/s per node, rough calc: each request might take ~0.3s so 3 requests/sec per node... math is fuzzy on call, but we'll run an exact sizing.
[06:25] Jordan: yep, we'll do a sizing table in the follow-up; that's part of the deliverables.
[06:30] Elena: any limit on model uploads? we want to host a fine-tuned variant and iterate quickly.
[06:36] Priya: you can manage model versions; deployment artifacts can be pinned. fine-tuned models are supported; we have safe model onboarding checklist.
[06:44] Rosa: what about data retention and logs - we want to ensure PII isn't stored in model cache or logs.
[06:49] Priya: we can configure prefix/KV cache policies and opt-out retention. for dedicated you have more controls; we'll outline recommended policies and defaults.
[06:58] Mark: practical question - how long to provision dedicated cluster for a pilot?
[07:03] Jordan: we can provision a small reserved pool within days for trial, depending on contractual approvals. for Private (VPC-on-prem) it takes longer - couple weeks for network setup.
[07:13] Samir: about backups - do you store KV caches across restarts? any encryption at rest?
[07:19] Priya: KV caches are optional persistent caches; encryption at rest via KMS. if you prefer ephemeral caches we can do that too.
[07:26] Mark: ok good. any customers in payments you can reference?
[07:30] Jordan: we have several fintech customers; i'll include anonymized case studies and performance notes. sometimes names get fuzzy in the transcript but we'll send references.
[07:40] Rosa: can we run benchmarks with our dataset?
[07:42] Priya: yes - we'll run a benchmark week on a trial pool. we'll need a representative prompt set, traffic patterns and business metrics (p95, throughput, cost per 1k).
[07:52] Elena: about SLA - we need uptime SLA and latency guarantees. do you offer SLAs on Dedicated?
[07:58] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets at enterprise tiers. we'll include service levels in the quote.
[08:06] Samir: also need contractual security appendices for regulated data - can provide a template.
[08:12] Jordan: we have a compliance pack; we'll share SOC2, pen-test summary, and network diagrams.
[08:17] Mark: anything else on burst strategy? can you do on-demand cloud bursting to our own GPUs?
[08:23] Priya: currently we support burst to Redwood-managed nodes; for hybrid set-ups we have Private on-prem options where you operate nodes and Redwood orchestrates. Cloud-burst-to-customer-owned infra is more custom but possible with integration work.
[08:38] Rosa: latency for embeddings - we have some batch jobs that run nightly, can we schedule cheaper preemptible nodes?
[08:45] Priya: yes, we offer lower-cost preemptible/spot burst nodes for non-latency-sensitive batch jobs. good fit for nightly embeddings.
[08:54] Mark: security again - SSO and provisioning - can we sync with our Okta and SCIM?
[09:01] Priya: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM provisioning are supported.
[09:06] Jordan: let's recap next steps before we run out of time.
[09:10] Jordan: action items: jordan send pricing and SLA options; priya to scope benchmark and sample prompts; elena to share traffic traces; samir to send compliance questions. we'll aim to provision trial next week pending approvals.
[09:24] Elena: thanks, we'll try to get docs to you by thursday.
[09:28] Mark: we want to see a TCO comparison and a clear migration plan from hosted api to dedicated.
[09:34] Jordan: we'll include a migration checklist and TCO spreadsheet.
[09:38] Rosa: can we get a 2-hour deep dive next tuesday for platform and app teams?
[09:43] Priya: yes, i'll send a calendar invite for technical deep dive + bench kickoff.
[09:48] Samir: thanks everyone.
[09:50] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and quotes.
